items.title: Rajnath Singh warns of evolving threats, calls for highest military readiness
points: The security landscape around the country has become increasingly complex and the armed forces must maintain the highest level of operational readiness to effectively counter any threats to national security, he told personnel at the Bagdogra Air Force…

Delivering his message on the eve of Deepavali from the key airbase near the frontier with China in the Eastern sector, Mr. Singh, without naming any country, said the adversary now avoids direct confrontation but seeks to exploit certain "vulnerabilities".

He called upon the armed forces to keep special focus on strengthening domain awareness, cyber resilience, and information integrity to effectively counter emerging security threats, according to the Defence Ministry.

Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Air Officer Commanding, Air Force Station, Bagdogra Air Commodore Manish Sharma, and other senior officials of the IAF were present on the occasion.

items.title: Nallur toll plaza on Kolkata National Highway to be moved to Durainallur
points: The National Highways Authority of India has planned to shift the toll plaza at Nallur on the Chennai - Kolkata National Highway.
It will be moved to Durainallur, which is about 13 km from the present location.
The plaza is notorious for long waits during rush hours.
Motorists fed up with waiting at the Nallur Plaza will get some relief from this move.
“Residents of areas such as Karanodai, Janapanchathiram, Nallur and Periyapalayam will find it very convenient when the plaza is removed.
It would be helpful if the road stretch is normalised and shops regularised,” he said.
Around 50,000 passenger car units use that road on a daily basis.
The plaza is also likely to be a multi-lane free flow tolling system without toll booths and operators.

items.title: Water released from Shenbagathoppu dam due to rain
points: The Shenbagathoppu dam reached around 80 percent of its storage capacity. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Due to continuous rain, water from Shenbagathoppu dam in Tiruvannamalai was released.

Officials of Water Resources Department (WRD), which maintains the dam, said around 100 cusecs of water per second from Shenbagathoppu dam was released as the dam reached around 80 percent of its total storage capacity.
At present, the water level in the dam is 56.24 ft as against its total storage capacity of 62.32 ft.
“As per norms, excess rainwater should be released when the dam nears 80% of its total storage capacity, to ensure safety of the structure.
Raja Ganapathy, Assistant Engineer (AE), WRD, told The Hindu.

Tiruvannamalai Collector Vandhana Garg has warned residents in Cheyyar, Arani, Vandavasi, and Polur towns along Kamandalam Naganathi river against crossing the waterbody as the waterflow in the river is on the rise.

items.title: Renovated bus terminus in Ranipet town opened for public use
points: Officials of Ranipet municipality, which executed the multi-crore work, said that the old terminus was built more than five decades ago with very few facilities for commuters.
“The restored terminus helps people board long-distance buses.
Funded under Kalaignar Nagarpura Membattu Thittam 2022-23 that aims to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in the urban local bodies, work to restore the terminus was started in 2022.
“The restored bus terminus will help commuters, especially women and senior citizens to board buses safely as round-the-clock surveillance is in place.
Senthil Kumar, Commissioner, Ranipet municipality.
The restored bus terminus will operate buses to Bengaluru, Vellore, Vandavasi, Cheyyar, Chengam, Arcot, Ranipet, Coimbatore, Salem, Kancheepuram, Hosur, and Dharmapuri.
Every day, on an average, more than 200 buses operated by Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation ply from the terminus.
Commuters said that additional buses to towns such as Tiruvannamalai, Sholinghur, Arcot, Gingee, and Kancheepuram should be operated at the terminus.

items.title: Greek-themed Salaam Souk to be held at Palace Grounds in Bengaluru on November 8
points: The Karnataka Tourism Department is supporting, ‘Salaam Souk – The Big Fat Greek Souk’, an event showcasing the colours, cuisine, music and Mediterranean culture of Greece to people in Bengaluru.
Scheduled to be held on November 8 in Palace Grounds, the event marks the eighth edition of Salaam Souk and its first Greek-themed edition.
It is an initiative of The Tribe & Co that has previously presented cultural themes inspired by Morocco, Turkey, Uzbekistan, India and Dubai.
The festival has been designed to recreate the feel of a Greek street market, combining Mediterranean-inspired food, fashion, art, music, home décor, beauty and wellness experiences.
The event will feature 35 food stalls, 150 retail stalls, live bands, fire shows and aerial performances, offering visitors a distinctive Greek-inspired cultural experience in Bengaluru.

items.title: Two youths arrested for possessing narcotics in Vellore
points: Two youths were arrested by Vellore South police for possession of 1300 narcotic tablets (Tapentadol) near the fort complex in Vellore town on Saturday.
Initial inquiry revealed that based on a tip-off to Vellore SP N.U.
Sivaraman, special teams were formed to conduct surprise checks in public places in the district.
During a surprise check near the fort complex, the team apprehended the suspects.
They checked the duo and their bags, where they found a huge quantity of pharmaceutical drugs in them.
A case was registered and arrested persons were lodged in Central Prison in Vellore.

items.title: Gang held near Vaniyambadi for burglary
points: A gang of five persons were arrested by Vaniyambadi Taluk police in Tirupattur on Saturday for stealing 52 sovereigns of gold jewellery, one kilogram of silver objects and around ₹20,000 lakh cash from the house of a painter recently.
The arrested persons were identified as K.
They are previous offenders and have theft cases against them in Salem, Dharmapuri, Tirupattur, Thanjavur, and Pudukottai.
Prabhakaran, 39, was living with his family including wife Geetha (34) and mother Ambika (65) in the house near Vaniyambadi town a few days ago when the gang barged into the house.
The police said the gang allegedly tied R.
Prabhakaran, 39, and his family and stole the valuables from the house before fleeing the spot.
Mr. Prabhakaran managed to untie himself and alerted Vaniyambadi Taluk police.
They travel to various parts of the State and stay in a locality before indulging in burglary.

items.title: T.N. may be heading towards a water crisis, unless northeast monsoon comes to the rescue
points: The State’s largest dam, Mettur, has about 23 thousand million cubic feet (tmcft) but this is hardly enough for the authorities to maintain sustained release of water to farmers, beyond a week, in the Cauvery delta. | Photo Credit: E.
LAKSHMI NARAYANAN Tamil Nadu may be in for a spell of water crisis and lower rice production this time, if the current Northeast monsoon does not come to its rescue.
In the corresponding period last year, the situation was completely different with the combined storage being around 92%.

The State’s largest dam, Mettur, has about 23 thousand million cubic feet (tmcft) but this is hardly enough for the authorities to maintain sustained release of water to farmers, beyond a week, in the Cauvery delta.
The rainfall during the Northeast monsoon has been moderate as the State has received around 240 mm of rainfall against the anticipated 236 mm.
Ordinarily, December yields only about 20% of the total rainfall of the monsoon.

items.title: ATMED, Anna University sign MoU to boost medical device industry-academia collaboration
points: According to a press release, the MoU was exchanged between V.
Kumaresan, registrar, Anna University, and Samuel William George, president, ATMED, at Anna University on November 3.

The partnership aims to bridge the gap between academic knowledge and industrial requirements through student internships, industry exposure, employment opportunities, technical training, research, product development, and technology commercialisation.
The collaboration will also promote joint workshops, seminars, faculty-industry interactions, student innovations, and opportunities to access Anna University’s technical infrastructure.

Through its network of member companies, ATMED will facilitate industrial exposure, mentorship and employment opportunities while supporting the development of skilled professionals and indigenous medical technologies, the release said.
Office bearers of ATMED and professors from the Biomedical Engineering Department, Anna University, were present on the occasion.

items.title: Bengal Minor Gives Birth In Nursing Home Toilet, Throws Baby Out Of Window
points: A minor girl allegedly threw her baby out of a nursing home's washroom window minutes after giving birth there, leading to its death in West Bengal's Hooghly district on Saturday, police said.

The incident took place after the 16-year-old girl was brought to the nursing home of Uttarpara Municipality by her family members late Friday night after she complained of severe abdominal pain, a senior officer of Uttarpara police station said.
"Initial investigation revealed that the girl went to the washroom on Saturday morning after complaining of intensifying abdominal pain.
She delivered a baby there without anybody's assistance," the officer said.
The nursing home authorities claimed that the minor allegedly threw the newborn out through the washroom window, he added.
"The family members had brought her to the nursing home believing that she was suffering from nothing more than a bout of ordinary abdominal pain.
Nursing home owner Sucheta Mukherjee told reporters that the minor was admitted late on Friday night and underwent a blood test on Saturday morning.

items.title: Inspired by Lord Ram's Journey, Noida Man Cycles 2,500 km From Rameswaram To Ayodhya
points: Inspired by Lord Ram's journey from Rameswaram to Ayodhya after defeating the demon king Ravan, a 30-year-old man from Noida has cycled 2,500 kilometres from Tamil Nadu to Uttar Pradesh in 16 days, crossing seven states, ahead of Diwali.
Speaking to PTI on Saturday, Sarthak Chauhan said he has been making this long journey for the third year in a row, calling it a "wonderful way to experience India's diversity and culture".
I cycled 2,500 kilometres from Rameswaram to Ayodhya in 16 days, crossing 7 states.
Like Lord Ram, who began his journey by offering prayers at Rameswaram after defeating Ravan on Dussehra, and arrived in Ayodhya in time for Diwali and Deepotsav, I, too, set out on the same path.
Every year, on Dussehra, we begin this journey after offering prayers at Rameswaram, and by Deepotsav, we reach Ayodhya," he said.
We will cycle to Ayodhya all the way from Rameswaram," he said, adding that people from Canada and England have evinced their interest in undertaking this journey.
